flagged.evidence: The step says to use “the first configuration on this run whose stack no longer begins with Z” and then asserts a factor ending with stack Yα. Take transitions (p,a,Z)->(s,W), (s,b,W)->(r,ε), and (r,c,Y)->(q,ε). The run (p,abc,ZY)->(s,bc,WY)->(r,c,Y)->(q,ε,ε) removes ZY. Its first configuration not beginning with Z is (s,bc,WY), not a configuration with stack Y, so the asserted factor (p,a,ZY)->*(s,ε,Y) does not exist.

The only cited local fact, [L1], comes from def-deterministic-pda, whose relevant assertion is only “A language is deterministic context-free when some DPDA recognizes it.” It does not license the claimed language-preserving “Kozen's endmarker repair,” the finite-DPDA “spurious-loop repair,” or the assertion that their macro-steps yield a total DPDA. Those substantial transformations are merely named in steps 1.1–2.1, with no local theorem or derivation establishing them; step 3.1 depends on them.

The construction says to “add a fresh start state with ε-transitions to the start states of N_L and N_K, and keep all old transitions and accepting states,” but does not require disjoint state sets. Let N_L have states {l,r,f_L}, start l, final f_L, and transitions l-a->r, r-a->f_L; let N_K have states {k,r,f_K}, start k, final f_K, and transitions k-b->f_K, r-c->f_K. They recognize {aa} and {b}. The stated merged construction accepts ac by taking the N_L branch to r and then N_K's r-c transition to f_K, although ac is not in {aa}∪{b}. Disjoint copies or state renaming are required.

Step 3.2 inducts on “the first time the current top symbol disappears” and says pushed fragments split according to [L3]. The cited lemma's step 1.2 makes the same invalid split. In the PDA with (p,a,Z)->(s,W), (s,b,W)->(r,ε), and (r,c,Y)->(q,ε), the top Z first disappears when it is replaced by W, leaving WY rather than the lower suffix Y. Thus that first event does not supply the claimed fragment factorization, so [L3] does not license the reverse-inclusion induction.
